title: Rapid fallback grid — sketch and user stories
content:
Quick note: this is a lightweight sketch for a fallback grid that proactively picks fallback strategies based on latency signals, user importance, and prompt shape. Intended as a product-prototype for hosted API routes where tail latency spikes or capacity pressure would otherwise cause high error rates or poor UX.

Context and why: we currently have ad-hoc fallbacks (model fallback to smaller model, simple retry) but they are route-level and coarse. Customer feedback: unpredictable quality when we switch to low-cost variants, and SRE wants predictable SLOs without brute force capacity scaling. Need a fine-grained policy layer that can pick among fallback actions with awareness of latency, cost, and user tier.

Core idea (one-liner): a 2D "fallback grid" where axes are latency risk (low/medium/high) and quality sensitivity (low/medium/high). Each cell maps to a prioritized list of fallback actions (e.g., reduce max_tokens, use cached prefix, switch to distilled model, degrade features like tool-calls, return partial/streamed response, graceful error). Policies can be per-route, per-tenant, and evaluated at request-time using lightweight signals.

Quick requirements / goals:
- Reduce 95th/99th percentile latency violations by 30% on noisy routes without increasing average token cost by >10%.
- Maintain observable quality regressions per prompt set; allow rollbacks via feature flags.
- Support per-tenant policy overrides for premium customers.
- Minimal added request latency for policy decision (<2ms).
- Play well with autoscaling and KV/prefix caches.

User stories (prioritized):
1) "As an end-user, I should get a timely, slightly lower-fidelity answer during platform congestion instead of a long wait or an error."
   - Acceptance: response returned < target latency 95% of the time, basic intent preserved in short-form summary.
2) "As a product engineer, I want to define per-route sensitivity so critical flows never degrade features like tool-calls."
   - Acceptance: route config exposed in Console; can mark features as non-degradable.
3) "As an SRE, I want fallback policies that reduce CPU/GPU load rapidly when tail queue depth rises so we avoid node OOMs."
   - Acceptance: fallbacks activate when queue length or QPS per GPU crosses thresholds; downstream GPU utilization reduces.
4) "As a platform operator, I want metrics showing which fallback cell made the decision and associated quality delta."
   - Acceptance: traceable via request logs and Console dashboard; ability to link to evaluation set.

Fallback actions (examples, not exhaustive):
- Prefix cache hit fast-path: return cached continuation with a confidence score.
- Shorten max_tokens / compress context: synthesize short summary of left-behind context (cheap compression heuristic).
- Model variant fallback: move to a quantized/distilled variant with known quality delta.
- Feature drop: disable tool-calls, remove external retrieval step.
- Streaming-partial: return first N tokens immediately and stream rest as background (with warning).
- Graceful degrade: return a structured short answer + suggestion to retry later.
- Hard error with recommended fallback: return 429/503 plus suggested lighter call (e.g., smaller model endpoint).

Signals to feed the policy (prioritized, lightweight):
- Per-request: prompt length, explicit priority header (x-rd-priority), route id, tenant id, latency budget header.
- Runtime signals: current queue depth for the model pool, 95/99 latency over 1 min rolling window, GPU mem pressure boolean, KV cache hit ratio.
- Historical signals: recent quality regression flag for model variant for that prompt set.

Policy model: simple rule engine plus a small ML cost-aware ranker for ordering fallbacks within a cell.
- Rule engine maps signals -> grid cell (latency_risk x quality_sensitivity). Implemented as a compact bitmap table for speed.
- Within-cell ranker orders actions by expected utility = (delta_latency_reduction / delta_quality_loss) weighted by tenant sensitivity. Ranker is trained from historical traces and updated weekly.

Config surface (Console + API):
- Per-route sensitivity (low/med/high), per-tenant overrides, global safeguard thresholds.
- Policy preview tool: run simulated trace on historic request batch to show expected fallback activations.
- Toggle: experimental rollout flag per-environment + canary percent.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Lab: simulate on recorded traces, run offline scoring, validate metrics (latency, cost, quality).
2) Internal canary: enable for internal tenants and low-traffic sandbox routes. Monitor 95/99 latency, error rate, token cost, human evals on curated prompts.
3) Customer alpha: opt-in for selected customers, collect qualitative feedback on UX differences.
4) Gradual ramp: default on for non-sensitive routes, tiered on for premium tenants.

Metrics to monitor (dashboard):
- Fallback activation rate by cell and route.
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) before vs after fallback.
- Token cost delta and revenue impact estimate.
- Quality regressions measured via micro-evals and customer-reported incidents.
- Rate of escalations / rollbacks.

Open questions / risks:
- How to measure "quality sensitivity" programmatically per route (heuristics vs explicit config)? Possible hybrid: default heuristics from route tags + explicit product override.
- Does the ML ranker add operational complexity? Start with deterministic ordering and add ranker later.
- Telemetry volume: need to ensure we don't blow up logging ingestion with fallback labels. Consider sampling.
- Interaction with Dedicated/Private modes: some fallbacks (model variant) may not be allowed in Private. Need config guardrails.

Experiment ideas (quick):
- A/B: cell-targeted A/B where 50% of traffic sees fallback grid and 50% uses baseline. Measure p95, errors, and micro-eval quality on a shared dataset.
- Offline simulate: run policy on last 7 days of traces and compute theoretical token savings and projected latency improvement.
- Tiny ML model: explore a cheap linear model to score action utility from latency+cost features.

Implementation notes (engineering sketch):
- Evaluate at API gateway level where request metadata is available. Keep decision stateless: pass short policy key to serving runtime which executes the action (e.g., choose model id, mute tool-calls).
- Use consistent hashing for model variant routing to preserve cache locality when possible.
- Persist per-request fallback decision in request context for auditing and replay.

Next steps (next 2 weeks):
- 1 pager for PM review with rough ROI calc (estimate token-savings vs potential quality impact).
- Prototype rule-engine + console UI mock for per-route sensitivity.
- Collect 7-day traces for candidate routes to run offline sim.

Notes to self: keep decisions auditable and reversible. Keep initial scope small: two routes (chat-short and long-completion) and one tenant class (standard). Avoid ML ranker in first iteration.

End of sketch — placeholder for more structured PRD once we validate offline sims and get SRE + customer success buy-in.
